summary: Verified iter_22 SEC-001 fix: narrative docx reader (phi_core/file_readers.py::read_docx) now enforces _DOCX_NARRATIVE_MAX_BYTES=10 MiB ZipInfo.file_size cap identical to the iter_20 dictionary-path defence. Ran targeted suite (tests/test_realworld_file_shapes.py) -> 11/11 PASSED including the 3 new iter_22 tests (oversize document.xml rejected, bad-zip returns empty, normal docx still parses). Ran full backend regression sweep (pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/e2e --ignore=tests/live --ignore=tests/test_agent_pipeline.py -q) -> 210 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failures in 22.43s. Matches expected result exactly. No regressions in dictionary-path reader.
critical_code_review_comments: Consider extracting the shared '10 MiB ZipInfo.file_size cap + defusedxml' logic between phi_core/file_readers.py::read_docx and phi_core/agents/specialists.py::_read_docx_tables into a small helper (e.g. _safe_open_docx_zip) to avoid future divergence — this SEC-001 was itself caused by the two readers drifting apart.
test_credentials: API_TOKEN empty by design (audit SEC-001 iter_18); no auth needed
seed_data_creation: None — all tests use tmp_path fixtures, no network, no LLM
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest with `python -m pytest` from /app/backend (not bare `pytest`) so phi_core resolves on sys.path — the repo has no pytest.ini/pyproject.toml. Full regression command: `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/e2e --ignore=tests/live --ignore=tests/test_agent_pipeline.py -q` (~22s, expect 210 passed / 4 skipped).
rca of the issue: SEC-001: dictionary-path docx reader was hardened in iter_20 with a ZipInfo.file_size cap + defusedxml, but the sibling narrative-path reader used by POST /upload -> /run was overlooked, leaving a decompression-bomb OOM vector via python-docx. iter_22 mirrors the exact same up-front ZipInfo.file_size <= 10 MiB check inside read_docx before python-docx opens the archive; on cap breach or bad ZIP the function returns '' so the pipeline degrades gracefully instead of OOMing. Verified by 3 new tests + full 210-test regression.
